title: A Flea Jumps 100 Times Its Body Length and Pulls Over 100 g

scenes.text: A flea jumps a hundred times its own body length.
Takeoff squeezes it with an acceleration of over a hundred g.
Astronauts feel about three g at launch. You'd pass out at five.
The secret is a springy protein called resilin in its legs.
It bends its leg for a tenth of a second to load the spring.
Then it fires in about a thousandth of a second.
A hundred body lengths, in a thousandth of a second.

description:
Fleas jump about a hundred times their body length with an acceleration of around 100 g or more.
They store energy in a springy protein called resilin.
Could you jump that far?
thumbnail_text: 100 G IN A THOUSANDTH OF A SECOND
